answer.answer: Based strictly on the supplied sources, exactly-once delivery cannot be confirmed as a reliable guarantee of Delta Queue. The documentation snapshot states that Delta Queue describes exactly-once delivery (delta-doc), but this is a documented claim, not verified behavior. The incident report provides empirical evidence contradicting that claim: during incident DQ-17, some messages were delivered twice (delta-incident), which is at-least-once behavior, not exactly-once. A conservative reading is therefore: (1) the vendor/documentation position is that exactly-once delivery is a described property (delta-doc); (2) at least one observed incident involved duplicate deliveries (delta-incident); (3) the duplicate deliveries during DQ-17 remain historically valid regardless of any later fixes; and (4) it is unresolved whether the guarantee holds today, whether DQ-17 predates or postdates the documentation, whether the incident was remediated, and whether the guarantee carries unstated conditions. No supplied source establishes the temporal ordering of the two snapshots or any remediation, so the documented claim and the observed incident must be treated as an unresolved contradiction rather than reconciled by inference. Enterprise guidance from these sources alone: do not treat exactly-once delivery as a verified guarantee; treat it as a documented claim with at least one recorded violation (DQ-17) pending further evidence.
